items.question: What is the optimal window for a comprehensive transabdominal fetal echocardiogram?
items.explanation: The optimal window is 18 to 22 weeks.

items.question: A mid-trimester fetal echocardiogram is normal and no progressive lesion is suspected. What follow-up does the guideline generally call for?
options: Repeat at 34 to 36 weeks in every case
items.explanation: A normal mid-trimester fetal echocardiogram generally needs no follow-up unless there is concern for a progressive lesion.

items.question: How often is an abnormal fetal heart usually reassessed?
options: Every 2 to 8 weeks until about 34 to 36 weeks, depending on the lesion
items.explanation: An abnormal heart is usually reassessed every 2 to 8 weeks until about 34 to 36 weeks, guided by the lesion and clinical concerns.

items.question: For pulmonary venous connections, what must a complete study show?
options: At least one vein from each side, on two-dimensional and colour imaging
All four veins on pulsed-wave Doppler
One vein on either side, on grey-scale only
items.explanation: The four-chamber assessment must show pulmonary venous connections from at least one vein on each side using two-dimensional and colour imaging; further veins are optional.

items.question: For the cardiac axis, what is required and what is optional?
options: Assessing the axis is required; measuring the angle is optional
Measuring the angle is required; assessing by eye is optional
The axis is assessed only with colour Doppler
items.explanation: The cardiac axis must be assessed in two dimensions; measuring the angle is optional.

items.question: Which measurement of heart size does a complete study require?
options: None; size is judged by eye only
items.explanation: A complete study requires a measured cardiac-to-thoracic area ratio.

items.question: Which view establishes whether the inferior vena cava is continuous?
items.explanation: The sagittal bicaval view establishes whether the inferior vena cava is continuous and whether both venae cavae lie on the same side.

items.question: What should colour Doppler demonstrate in the three-vessel-and-trachea view?
options: Patency and direction of flow in both arches
The peak velocity in the aortic arch
items.explanation: Colour Doppler should demonstrate patency and flow direction in both arches.

items.question: A standard view cannot be obtained. When can the study still count as complete?
options: When every cardiovascular structure has been adequately seen by another approach, or is anatomically absent
When at least half the views were obtained
When the four-chamber view was normal
items.explanation: The study is complete only if all cardiovascular structures are adequately seen by another approach or are anatomically absent.

items.question: The study is still non-diagnostic after every adjustment. What should the report do?
options: Leave out the views not seen without comment
items.explanation: If the study remains non-diagnostic after optimisation, the report should identify the limitations.

items.question: Which two assessments must every fetal echocardiogram include, beyond anatomy?
options: Heart rate and rhythm, and a qualitative assessment of systolic and diastolic function
Middle cerebral artery Doppler and cervical length
Myocardial performance index and cardiovascular profile score
items.explanation: Every study must document rate and rhythm and include a qualitative assessment of systolic and diastolic function.

items.question: Which view, with colour Doppler added, can show muscular ventricular septal defects?
items.explanation: The low short-axis view can show muscular ventricular septal defects when colour Doppler is added.
